bugs.error_message: Shopify connection page showed "Failed — Missing read_products scope" even though product import/sync was actually working
bugs.root_cause: ShopifyAuthService::testConnection() hard-gated the ENTIRE result on `str_contains($token['scope'], 'read_products')` — a check against the OAuth token response's self-reported scope STRING — before ever attempting the real GET /products.json call. If Shopify's client_credentials grant response formats/omits the scope string differently than expected, this false-negatived the whole connection even when the real API call would have succeeded.
bugs.fix: Did not touch ShopifyAuthService (task: don't rewrite Shopify auth architecture; also has its own passing test suite). Added a new, separate ShopifyCapabilityDiagnosticsService + "Run diagnostics" UI/endpoint that determines every READ capability from a real, safe (non-mutating) Shopify Admin API call's actual HTTP status (200/401/403) — never from the scope string. Write capabilities are reported from scopes only (never mutation-tested, per explicit safety requirement) and are surfaced as their own 'configured'/'not_configured' status, never folded into a pass/fail gate. Connection-level status is now 3-way (connected/partially_configured/failed) and is explicitly never 'failed' when products.read passed.

bugs.error_message: Clicking Publish on a product imported from WooCommerce also pushed it to Shopify whenever the store had an active Shopify connection, even though the user never selected Shopify
bugs.root_cause: ProductController::push() (now removed) grabbed every active PlatformConnection for the store (`$store->connections()->where('status','active')->get()`), grouped by platform, and pushed to all of them unconditionally — there was no concept of a user-selected target at all. The Edit page's "Publish to platforms" button called this route with an empty body.
bugs.fix: Replaced push()/`/push` with publish()+bulkPublish() (`/publish`, `/bulk-publish`), both requiring an explicit, validated `connection_ids` array. New App\Services\Sync\ProductPublishService orchestrates: resolves only connections that belong to the product's own store, checks ProductChannelListing per connection (update if linked, skip with `not_linked_to_channel` unless `create_missing_listings` is true), and never touches a platform the caller didn't name. ProductPushService::pushProduct()/createProduct()/createVariableProduct() gained an optional `$connectionIds` param (defaults to null = old behavior, for any other existing caller) so the orchestrator can scope to exact connections instead of "every connection for a platform". Frontend: both Edit.jsx and Index.jsx now open a PublishTargetModal (default selection: none) instead of posting immediately.

bugs.error_message: Shopify integration page could show a green "Synced" badge and a red "Token is missing the read_products scope" error at the same time
bugs.root_cause: Two independent bugs compounded: (1) backend — ShopifyAuthService::requestToken() called markValid() as soon as ANY non-empty scope came back, before testConnection() went on to check for the specific read_products scope or make the real products.json call; those later checks returned ok:false to the caller but never called markFailed() to correct the already-persisted token_status:'valid'. (2) frontend — the verification panel rendered its StatusBadge from the stale page-load `connection.token_status` prop while rendering the error message from a separately-sourced, ephemeral `testResult` state set only by the just-completed axios response; the two had no way to agree with each other.
bugs.fix: Backend: every exit path of testConnection() (domain invalid, credentials rejected/401, empty scope, missing read_products, products-endpoint 403/401/other, and true success) now calls markValid()/markFailed() with the task-specified exact wording, so exactly one final state is ever persisted per test run. Frontend: dropped the separate testResult state entirely; after a test-connection call, the page does `router.reload({only:['connection']})` and the badge+message are both derived from one computed `state` variable (untested/connected/failed) off the freshly-reloaded `connection` prop — structurally impossible to show both at once. Badge label also renamed Synced->Connected/Failed/Untested.

bugs.error_message: Clicking 'Publish to platforms' on a product that IS linked via ProductChannelListing but never had the deprecated Product.external_id column set silently no-ops ("Product is already linked to this channel") instead of pushing the edited fields to WooCommerce/Shopify/YouCan
bugs.root_cause: push() decided create-vs-update per PLATFORM GROUP using the single legacy Product.external_id flag ($product->external_id ? pushProduct() : createProduct()), not the per-connection ProductChannelListing. createProduct() correctly detects an existing listing and skips (by design, that's pushProduct()'s job) but returns success without pushing any field changes — so a product whose only mapping is the modern channel-listing table (the normal state after Option B2's product migration, or any product synced without external_id ever being backfilled) always took the create branch and never actually updated the remote product.
bugs.fix: push() now decides per platform group via $product->listingForConnection()/externalIdForConnection() on that platform's connection (unique per store+platform) instead of the global legacy flag. Discovered while writing WooCommerceOutboundSyncTest's 'publishes product changes using the existing remote product id' test — Http::assertSent() found zero requests because createProduct() had short-circuited.

bugs.error_message: "Something went wrong: Undefined array key \"description\"" flashed on product create/update whenever an optional field (description/category/compare_price/cost/featured_image) is omitted from the request
bugs.root_cause: store()/update() read $validated['description'] etc. directly instead of with a ?? fallback, even though those keys are validated as 'nullable' — Laravel's $request->validate() omits a nullable key entirely from the returned array when it isn't present in the request at all (as opposed to present-but-null). It was latent because Create.jsx/Edit.jsx's useForm() always initializes those fields to '' so the browser always sends them; a minimal API-style POST (e.g. from tests) without those keys hit it immediately.
bugs.fix: Changed every optional field read to '$validated["x"] ?? null' (and the compare_price/cost ternaries to check '($validated["x"] ?? null)' before casting) in both store() and update().

bugs.error_message: TypeError: App\Http\Controllers\Settings\SettingsController::profileRules(): Argument #1 ($userId) must be of type ?int, string given — 500 on PATCH /settings/profile
bugs.root_cause: profileRules()/emailRules() were typed '?int $userId' (auto-increment assumption), but this app uses ULID string primary keys everywhere. The bug was latent and never exercised because the old Volt settings pages 500'd earlier (broken <x-pages::settings.layout> component) before validation ever ran — the new SettingsController (Option B1 migration) was the first real caller to pass $user->id (a ULID string) through.
bugs.fix: Widened profileRules()/emailRules() signatures to 'string|int|null $userId = null' in app/Concerns/ProfileValidationRules.php. No caller changes needed.

bugs.error_message: Dashboard stock adjustment for a variable product doesn't let you pick which variant gets the stock; increments land on the parent product row and don't sync to the correct variant in the POS
bugs.root_cause: StockController::adjustStock hardcoded 'variant_id' => null in Stock::firstOrCreate (line 84), so every dashboard adjustment wrote the product-level stock row regardless of variant. index() also sent no variant data to Stock.jsx, and AdjustStockModal only had a single quantity input — the UI could not offer a variant choice. stock_ledger had no variant_id column so history couldn't attribute a change to a variant.
bugs.fix: index() now eager-loads variants with sellable stock_sum (whereHas warehouse.sellable) and presents { type, has_variants, variant_count, variants:[{id,name,sku,stock}] } via paginator->through(). adjustStock() accepts batch payload { reason, notes, adjustments:[{variant_id,quantity_change}] }, validates that variable products target a real owned variant (and simple products carry null), skips zero rows, and writes each delta to the exact (product,variant,warehouse) Stock row + a variant-tagged StockLedger entry (applyAdjustment helper, one DB transaction). Added variant_id to stock_ledger (migration 2026_07_26_000002) + StockLedger fillable/relation. Frontend: rewrote AdjustStockModal.jsx — simple products keep the single input; variable products get a scrollable per-variant list (name/sku, current stock, signed input, live current→new preview, filter box when >6 variants), submit-disabled until a non-zero row exists. Stock.jsx cards + StockMovements.jsx rows show a variants badge. Sync to POS is automatic: both read the same sellable `stocks` rows (POS presentProduct stock_sum), reflected on the POS's next fetch/search (no websocket push).

bugs.error_message: POS: clicking a variable product (with sizes/colors) failed / added it directly with no way to pick the specific variant
bugs.root_cause: presentProduct() only returned id/name/sku/price/images/stock — it never included variants or attributes. Variable products arrived at the React POS looking identical to simple ones, so onAdd(product) added the BASE product row (base price, aggregate variant stock) via useCart, and cart lines were keyed by product_id alone, so a variant could never be distinguished or chosen. adjustInventory() also hardcoded variant_id => null, so even if a variant sold, the wrong (product-level) Stock row was decremented.
bugs.fix: Backend: presentProduct now eager-loads variants.attributeValues + sellable stock_sum and returns { type, has_variants, variant_count, price_from, attributes:[{name,values}], variants:[{id,name,sku,price,stock,image,options}] }. Added variant_id to pos_order_items (migration 2026_07_26_000001), PosOrderItem fillable+relation, CheckoutController validation (items.*.variant_id nullable exists), OrderProcessingService persists variant_id and decrements the matching variant Stock row. Frontend: new VariantModal.jsx (attribute pill selectors, per-combination live stock, out-of-stock disabling relative to other selections, qty stepper), useCart keyed by composite line_id (`${productId}::${variantId}`) with addItem(product,{variant,quantity}); Dashboard opens the modal for has_variants products (adds simple ones directly) and folds the variant label into the receipt line name; ProductCard/CartItem/Cart/CheckoutPreviewModal made variant-aware.

bugs.error_message: Clicking Connect/Configure on the Integrations page 404s — user reported the connection flow never opens
bugs.root_cause: The Connect button linked to `/stores/${store.id}/connections/connect` and Configure to `/stores/${store.id}/connections`. Those `stores.connections.*` routes belonged to the old Livewire ConnectPlatform wizard, which was DELETED on the cleanup/orphaned-blade branch (see cerebrum 'Connector architecture legacy stack REMOVED'). The Integrations UI was migrated to per-platform Inertia pages (Dashboard/Integrations/Platforms/{WooCommerce,Shopify,YouCan,WhatsApp}.jsx) served at /dashboard/integrations/{platform}, but Index.jsx's two buttons were never repointed, so every Connect/Configure click hit a non-existent URL.
bugs.fix: Repointed both <Link> hrefs in Index.jsx to `/dashboard/integrations/${p.key}`. The provider keys (woocommerce/shopify/youcan/whatsapp) already equal the registered route path segments (verified via `route:list --path=dashboard/integrations`: all four GET routes exist). Connect and Configure share the same per-platform page — it renders the credential form for a new connection and shows 'Update credentials' when already connected. No backend/route change needed; the routes and controller were already correct.

bugs.error_message: SQLSTATE[42000]: 1059 Identifier name 'product_variant_attribute_values_product_variant_id_product_attribute_value_id_unique' is too long — migrate:fresh aborted at pvav; 38 later migrations sat Pending in the real DB and never ran
bugs.root_cause: The original 61-file migration set could not build a fresh MySQL database. 2026_05_25_000003 created product_variant_attribute_values with $table->unique(['product_variant_id','product_attribute_value_id']) — Laravel's auto-generated index name exceeded MySQL's 64-char limit, so migrate:fresh died there and every migration after it (POS, factures, teams, returns, all the ALTERs) never executed. Separately, several ALTER migrations used native ENUM MODIFY guarded only for mysql, and the committed extend_sync_logs_action_enum lacked the sqlite guard (fails on the sqlite test DB).
bugs.fix: Squashed 61 migrations into 34 clean create-table migrations (one per table), each reflecting the FINAL schema with every add/rename/drop/widen folded in. pvav now uses a composite PRIMARY KEY named 'pvav_primary' (product_variant_id, product_attribute_value_id) — it enforces uniqueness on its own, so the over-long unique index is gone. Evolving lists (orders/pos_orders.fulfillment_status, inventory_adjustments.source) are created as their final VARCHAR; sync_logs.action and factures.status are created with their final ENUM value sets; activity_log morph ids are char(26) from the start. FK dependency order preserved via timestamps (only reorder: store_roles before store_members/store_invitations). Data-only migrations dropped (no-ops on a fresh DB). Verified: migrate:fresh builds all 40 tables cleanly on MySQL; Pest suite 189 pass / 7 pre-existing failures (onboarding-redirect + deleted settings.profile component on the cleanup branch, unrelated to schema). Extracted ground truth via a throwaway scratch DB (saas_squash_tmp); the real saas_commerce dev DB was never touched.

bugs.error_message: Synced WooCommerce orders all collapse onto ONE row (new orders take older orders' data); re-sync also resets an order's status back to Pending every minute
bugs.root_cause: 1) WooCommerceConnector::parseOrder returned 'external_id'/'order_number' but BaseConnector::normalizeOrder reads 'platform_id'/'number' with no fallback -> platform_id='' for every WC order. The unique key (platform_connection_id, platform_order_id) then matched the single ('conn','') row, so every order overwrote it (Shopify/YouCan were fine — they emit platform_id). 2) OrderSyncService::saveOrder used updateOrCreate and set status=OrderStatus::Pending in the values on EVERY sync, resetting the commercial status of already-advanced orders and clobbering their volatile fields.
bugs.fix: WooCommerceConnector::parseOrder now emits 'platform_id'/'number'; normalizeOrder falls back to external_id/order_number defensively. saveOrder rewritten: returns ?Order; skips (logs) empty platform_id; looks up existing by (connection,platform_order_id); if it exists and fulfillment_status !== Pending it is left untouched (SaaS owns the lifecycle), if still Pending only volatile platform data is refreshed (never status); new orders are Order::create'd with status=Pending AND fulfillment_status=Pending (awaiting confirmation) then fire OrderCreated + SendWhatsAppConfirmation. syncFromPlatform loop skips null returns. Tests: tests/Feature/Orders/OrderSyncServiceTest.php (6). NOTE: there is NO order webhook — sync is poll-only; both scheduler and SyncPlatformOrders job share this saveOrder path. Existing single empty-platform_order_id row from the old bug can be deleted manually.

bugs.error_message: Scheduled sync failed: OrderSyncService::syncFromPlatform(): Argument #3 ($since) must be of type ?Carbon\Carbon, Carbon\CarbonImmutable given, called in routes/console.php on line 24
bugs.root_cause: AppServiceProvider.php:109 sets Date::use(CarbonImmutable::class) globally, so every model datetime cast and now() returns CarbonImmutable. The scheduler passes $connection->last_synced_at->subMinutes(5) (a CarbonImmutable) into syncFromPlatform(), whose $since param was hinted ?Carbon\Carbon. CarbonImmutable is NOT a subclass of Carbon (both are siblings under CarbonInterface), so the TypeError fired. The connectors' getOrders(?Carbon $since) had the same too-narrow hint downstream.
bugs.fix: Widened $since to ?Carbon\CarbonInterface in OrderSyncService::syncFromPlatform and getOrders across BaseConnector (abstract) + all three connectors (import changed Carbon\Carbon -> Carbon\CarbonInterface; Carbon was used nowhere else in those files). CarbonInterface is the shared parent so it accepts both mutable and immutable. Verified by reflection + full suite (225/183, 7 pre-existing).

bugs.error_message: SQLSTATE[23000]: Integrity constraint violation: 1452 ... stocks_product_id_foreign ... insert into stocks (product_id, ...) values (7778, ...) — confirming an online (WooCommerce) order threw a FK violation
bugs.root_cause: OrderLineItems::fromOnline() copied product_id/variant_id straight from the orders.items JSON blob, but that blob stores the PLATFORM's ids (e.g. WooCommerce product id 7778), not local ULIDs. On confirm, OrderWorkflowService::applyStockEffects() -> StockMovementWriter::move(productId:'7778') tried to firstOrCreate a stocks row whose product_id (7778) has no matching products.id (all ULIDs) -> FK 1452. The class docblock already promised product_id was the LOCAL id (nullable when unmatched); fromOnline violated that. Also latently affected ReturnInspectionService (other OrderLineItems::for consumer).
bugs.fix: fromOnline() now resolves each raw id (platform external_id OR an already-local ULID) to the local product/variant ULID via batched lookups (localProductMap/localVariantMap, scoped to order store_id, matching external_id OR id). Unmatched -> null, so StockMovementWriter::move() skips it (its productId===null guard). POS path (fromPos) unchanged — pos_order_items.product_id is already a local FK. Regression tests added to tests/Feature/Orders/OrderWorkflowServiceTest.php: (1) platform external_id 7778 resolves + deducts stock, (2) unmatched id moves no stock and does not throw.

bugs.error_message: SyncPlatformOrders job + SyncService::syncOrders()/testConnection() have stale signatures; dispatching the job or calling those methods throws TypeError
bugs.root_cause: OrderSyncService::syncFromPlatform() changed to require (Store, PlatformConnection, ?Carbon) and ConnectorFactory exposes only static make(PlatformConnection); SyncService::syncOrders() still passes a string platform, and testConnection() calls a non-existent factory->create(). SyncPlatformOrders::handle() calls syncOrders($platformConnection) with wrong arity/type. The live order-sync path is the every-minute scheduler in routes/console.php calling OrderSyncService directly.
bugs.fix: FIXED 2026-07-26: SyncService::syncOrders(Store,string) now resolves the store's PlatformConnection and calls OrderSyncService::syncFromPlatform($store,$connection), returning the SyncLog; testConnection() type-hinted to PlatformConnection and uses static ConnectorFactory::make($conn)->authenticate() (unused injected ConnectorFactory removed from constructor); SyncPlatformOrders::handle() now injects OrderSyncService and calls syncFromPlatform($conn->store,$conn) directly, mirroring the scheduler. Suite unchanged (181 pass / 7 pre-existing). Note: the only remaining callers of testConnection()/SyncPlatformOrders::dispatch() are the dead unrouted Livewire EditConnection/ConnectionIndex, pending the step-2 Blade sweep.

bugs.error_message: Shopify variant created without option values (L/Red attributes not appearing)

bugs.error_message: WooCommerce variation attributes silently ignored — size/color not appearing on variation
bugs.root_cause: WooCommerce requires the parent product to have variation attributes defined (variation:true) before a variation can be linked to them. Creating a variation with attributes the parent doesn't know about is silently accepted but the attributes are discarded.
bugs.fix: Added syncParentProductAttributes() helper that GETs the product, checks for missing/incomplete attribute definitions, and PUTs the updated attributes back before creating/updating the variation.

bugs.error_message: Wrong reference: ProductEdit should be ProductEditWizard
SQLSTATE[23000]: Integrity constraint violation: 1062 Duplicate entry 'TEST-9-QF...' for key 'product_variants_sku_unique'
bugs.root_cause: finalize() is called twice in one wizard session: openPushModal() calls finalize('draft'), then confirmPush() calls finalize('active'). The first call soft-deletes existing variants then creates new ones with SKUs like TEST-9-QF. The second call soft-deletes those variants (deleted_at set) but MySQL unique index still sees the soft-deleted rows — INSERT of the same SKU on re-creation throws 1062. Additionally, product_variants.sku had a global UNIQUE constraint instead of per-product (product_id, sku), which is the wrong business rule.
bugs.fix: 1. Removed finalize('draft') from openPushModal() — replaced with autosave() so variants are only persisted once by confirmPush()->finalize('active'). 2. Changed finalize() variant deletion from deleteWithStock() (soft-delete) to forceDelete() after deleting StockMovements and Stocks manually, freeing the unique index slots. 3. Added migration 2026_05_26_000001 to change unique(sku) to unique(product_id, sku) — variant SKUs are unique per-product, not globally.

bugs.error_message: Product images never appear in the UI for any platform after sync
bugs.root_cause: Two-part issue: (1) Shopify and YouCan connectors emitted 'image_url' in their parsed payload, but ProductSyncService::saveProduct() only reads 'featured_image' — the key mismatch silently dropped the URL on every sync. WooCommerce was unaffected because it already returned 'featured_image'. (2) product-index.blade.php never rendered an image column, so even WooCommerce rows that did persist featured_image were invisible.
bugs.fix: Normalized Shopify + YouCan parseProduct() to return 'featured_image' (matching WooCommerce and what ProductSyncService consumes). Added extractYouCanFeaturedImage()/extractYouCanImages() helpers that read images[].url (the YouCan API shape) with thumbnail/image fallbacks. Added thumbnail_url accessor on Product model (returns images[1] if present, else featured_image). Added a 40px thumbnail column to product-index.blade.php with loading=lazy, onerror fallback, alt text, and a placeholder SVG when no image exists.

bugs.error_message: [plugin:vite:css] [postcss] It looks like you're trying to use `tailwindcss` directly as a PostCSS plugin. The PostCSS plugin has moved to a separate package
bugs.root_cause: Project was half-migrated from Tailwind v3 to v4. tailwindcss@4.0.7 and @tailwindcss/vite@4.1.11 were installed but unused: vite.config.js never wired @tailwindcss/vite, postcss.config.js still used 'tailwindcss: {}' (v4 split that into @tailwindcss/postcss), and app.css still used @tailwind base/components/utilities directives. @tailwindcss/forms was referenced from tailwind.config.js but not installed.
bugs.fix: 1) Wired @tailwindcss/vite into vite.config.js plugins[]. 2) Deleted postcss.config.js entirely (the Vite plugin replaces it). 3) Replaced @tailwind directives in app.css with @import "tailwindcss" + @config "../../tailwind.config.js" so the v3-style JS config (forms, darkMode:class, Inter, content globs) is still honored. 4) npm install @tailwindcss/forms.

bugs.error_message: Error: Cannot apply unknown utility class `btn` (from @tailwindcss/vite:generate:build)
bugs.root_cause: In Tailwind v4, @apply inside @layer components cannot resolve another custom class (e.g. .btn-primary doing @apply btn bg-blue-600). v3 allowed this implicitly; v4 enforces strict utility resolution and components-layer classes are not registered as utilities.
bugs.fix: Converted every @layer components { .name { @apply ... } } block to @utility name { @apply ...; }. The @utility directive registers the class so other utilities can @apply it. @layer base was kept for element selectors, scrollbar styling, and [x-cloak]. Vite build now produces 137 KB CSS with no errors.

bugs.root_cause: fulfillment_status on orders + pos_orders was created as a native ENUM over 5 states. The order lifecycle needed 10 (confirmed, delivered, returned, under_inspection, return_completed). MySQL silently truncates values outside an ENUM; Laravel 13 SQLiteGrammar::typeEnum() compiles to varchar check(col in (...)), so the in-memory test DB rejects them too - the test suite would have failed differently rather than catching the production bug.

MODIFY VARCHAR(32) for mysql/mariadb only (no-op on fresh DBs, skipped on SQLite) plus (store_id, fulfillment_status) indexes. App\Enums\FulfillmentStatus now does the validating. Verified by migrating a scratch SQLite DB and a test that persists all 10 states.

bugs.error_message: A newly created secondary warehouse does not appear in the Source/Destination dropdowns of the Stock Transfer form — only the default warehouse shows.
bugs.root_cause: Two competing notions of 'the store's warehouses'. WarehouseController::store() creates a Warehouse with user_id but NEVER attaches it to the warehouse_store pivot. The Warehouses list page queries by user_id (so it shows there), but all stock features — StockTransferController's warehousePayload/availability, Store::getPrimaryWarehouse/getDamagedWarehouse — read the pivot ($store->warehouses()). Only the auto-created default attaches itself, so a manually created warehouse is invisible to transfers. The frontend dropdown was already dynamic (warehouses.map) — not the cause.
bugs.fix: Added Store::attachOwnerWarehouses() (idempotent; attaches warehouses owned by the store's user that are attached to NO store via whereDoesntHave('stores'), so it never steals another store's warehouse) and Store::markPrimaryWarehouse(). WarehouseController::store() now attaches the new warehouse to the active store (and honors is_default by marking it primary). StockTransferController::create() calls attachOwnerWarehouses() to self-heal already-orphaned warehouses on page load. Tests: 3 new in StockTransferTest (7 total).

bugs.error_message: On the Order management board (/dashboard/orders/manage) clicking the 'Direct POS' source tab returns no orders even though test POS orders exist
bugs.root_cause: The board filters orders by the active department's phases BEFORE the source tab applies. The default 'All open' department only included phases ['confirmation','fulfillment','returns']. Instant POS sales are created as FulfillmentStatus::Completed whose phase() is 'closed', so every completed POS order was filtered out before the POS source tab could match. A second latent bug: COLUMNS mislabelled ready_for_delivery/delivered as phase 'fulfillment' while the enum phase() returns 'delivery', and no department listed the 'delivery' phase, so delivery-stage orders were dropped from the source/department tallies too.
bugs.fix: Renamed the default department to 'All orders' and gave it every phase ['confirmation','fulfillment','delivery','returns','closed'] so completed POS sales are visible and the Direct POS tab returns them. Corrected COLUMNS phase for ready_for_delivery/delivered to 'delivery' and added 'delivery' to the Fulfillment + All departments (matches App\Enums\FulfillmentStatus::phase). Bumped the board grid fallback to xl:grid-cols-5 so the wider 'All orders' view wraps cleanly. Also added a unified server-filtered orders LIST at /dashboard/orders (OrderController@index) merging POS+Online with a working Source filter as the canonical browse view.

bugs.error_message: Order management UI: 'Pending / delivery' (a workflow stage) shows in the SOURCE column; clicking the 'Direct POS' source tab shows 0 orders / 'No orders match this view' even though POS orders exist
bugs.root_cause: OrderPresenter::pos() overloaded the `source` field with the delivery FULFILLMENT concept: for a POS delivery order (status==='pending_delivery') it emitted source='delivery' + source_label='Pending / delivery' instead of the real channel. Two consequences: (1) the Source column/badge rendered the workflow stage 'Pending / delivery' — a status, not a channel; (2) the board's Direct POS tab filters `o.source !== 'pos'`, and POS delivery orders carried source='delivery', so they were excluded — a store whose POS orders are all delivery-type showed 0 under Direct POS. This sat on top of the earlier bug-manage-board-pos-filter-hides-orders (department-phase) fix; this is the deeper modeling defect.
bugs.fix: Made `source` strictly the sales channel: OrderPresenter::pos() now always emits source='pos'/source_label='Direct POS' and moves the delivery signal to new dedicated fields is_delivery/fulfillment_type/fulfillment_label; online() gained the same fulfillment_* fields. Manage.jsx: dropped the 'delivery' source tab (source tabs are now All/Direct POS/Online store), removed delivery from SOURCE_TONE and the bySource tally, and the drawer 'Fulfillment' row now reads fulfillment_label (Instant pickup / Delivery / later) instead of source_label. Packing.jsx: its 'POS delivery' queue tab now filters on source='pos' (in the packing phase the only POS orders present are delivery ones) instead of the retired source='delivery'. useQueue.js source-union comment updated. POS creation (OrderProcessingService) already sets status/fulfillment_status correctly via FulfillmentType and a pos_orders row is inherently the POS channel, so no schema/source column was added. PosDeliveryRoutingTest updated to assert source==='pos'/source_label==='Direct POS'/is_delivery. Tests: PosDeliveryRouting 5/5, OrderChannelViews+Department 39/39 green (9 OrderManagementTest failures are pre-existing orphaned-Livewire-view errors on the cleanup branch, unrelated).
